stem: Which statement regarding Benign Chronic Neutropenia of childhood is true?

options.text: It is a genetic condition that is present at birth and requires lifelong GCSF.
It is thought to be an immune-mediated process that typically resolves by preschool age.
It is always associated with severe, life-threatening bacterial sepsis.
It is caused by a profound deficiency in dietary Vitamin $B_{12}$.

explanation: This condition is common in infants and toddlers and is characterized by low neutrophil counts that improve as the immune system matures.
rationale: Consider the 'benign' nature and the typical age range for resolution.

optionExplanations.A: This describes severe congenital neutropenia; benign chronic neutropenia is acquired and often resolves on its own.
optionExplanations.B: This condition is common in infants and toddlers and is characterized by low neutrophil counts that improve as the immune system matures.
optionExplanations.C: While it can occasionally lead to infections, many children are asymptomatic and the neutropenia is found incidentally.
optionExplanations.D: Nutritional deficiencies are a separate cause of neutropenia and would typically present with other hematological abnormalities like macrocytosis.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: It is thought to be an immune-mediated process that typically resolves by preschool age.
